items.subject: eng

skill.en: Agreeing to a request for help
skill.th: การตอบรับคำขอความช่วยเหลือ

topic.th: บทสนทนาในชีวิตประจำวัน

items.stem:
Choose the best response to complete the conversation.
A: Could you give me a hand with these boxes? They're heavier than they look.
B: ______ Where do you want them?

explanation.en: B then asks where to put the boxes, so B is agreeing: "Sure, no problem". "No, I couldn't" refuses, "Help yourself" invites someone to take something, and "Give me a break" means stop bothering me.
explanation.th: B ถามต่อว่าจะให้วางกล่องที่ไหน แสดงว่ายินดีช่วย จึงตอบ Sure, no problem ส่วน No, I couldn't เป็นการปฏิเสธ Help yourself ใช้เชิญให้หยิบเอง และ Give me a break แปลว่าอย่ากวนใจ

items.subject: eng

skill.th: การแนะนำไม่ให้ทำบางสิ่ง

topic.th: บทสนทนาในชีวิตประจำวัน

items.stem:
Choose the best response to complete the conversation.
A: I'm thinking of dyeing my hair bright blue for the school festival.
B: ______ The school rules say natural colours only.
choices: I wouldn't do that if I were you.
That sounds like a brilliant idea.

explanation.en: B mentions a rule against unnatural colours, so B is warning A not to do it: "I wouldn't do that if I were you". The other three all encourage the idea.
explanation.th: B อ้างกฎโรงเรียนที่ห้ามย้อมสีผมไม่เป็นธรรมชาติ จึงเป็นการเตือน I wouldn't do that if I were you อีกสามตัวเลือกล้วนสนับสนุนความคิดนั้น

items.subject: eng

skill.th: การตอบคำถาม Is this seat taken?

topic.th: บทสนทนาในชีวิตประจำวัน

items.stem:
Choose the best response to complete the conversation.
A: Excuse me, is this seat taken?
B: ______ My friend has just gone to buy some drinks.

explanation.en: The friend is coming back, so the seat is taken: "I'm afraid it is" says yes politely. "No, feel free" and "Not that I know of" say it is free, and "Yes, please sit down" contradicts itself.
explanation.th: เพื่อนของ B กำลังจะกลับมา ที่นั่งจึงมีคนจองแล้ว I'm afraid it is เป็นการตอบรับอย่างสุภาพ ส่วน No, feel free และ Not that I know of บอกว่าว่าง และ Yes, please sit down ขัดแย้งในตัวเอง

items.subject: eng

skill.th: การยอมรับคำวิจารณ์

topic.th: บทสนทนาในชีวิตประจำวัน

items.stem:
Choose the best response to complete the conversation.
A: You look exhausted. Have you been up all night?
B: Pretty much. I had to finish my history report.
A: Again? You really should stop leaving things until the last minute.
B: ______ I'll start the next one the day it's set.

explanation.en: B promises to start earlier next time, so B accepts the criticism: "Point taken" (= I understand and accept what you said). "Mind your own business" rejects it rudely, "Speak for yourself" says the comment applies to A, and "So do I" makes no sense here.
explanation.th: B สัญญาว่าจะเริ่มทำงานเร็วขึ้น แสดงว่ายอมรับคำติ จึงตอบ Point taken (รับทราบและยอมรับ) ส่วน Mind your own business เป็นการปฏิเสธอย่างหยาบ Speak for yourself หมายถึงคนพูดเองต่างหาก และ So do I ไม่เข้ากับบริบท

items.subject: eng

skill.th: การปลอบใจโดยใช้สำนวน

topic.th: บทสนทนาในชีวิตประจำวัน

items.stem:
Choose the best response to complete the conversation.
A: How was the job interview?
B: I think I blew it. I was so nervous that I couldn't think straight.
A: ______ You never know—maybe they liked you more than you think.
choices: You've hit the nail on the head.
Don't be so hard on yourself.

explanation.en: A is comforting B, so "Don't be so hard on yourself" (= don't criticise yourself so much) fits. "Hit the nail on the head" means you are exactly right, which would agree B failed; "Better late than never" and "the last straw" do not fit the situation.
explanation.th: A กำลังปลอบใจ B จึงใช้ Don't be so hard on yourself (อย่าโทษตัวเองมากนัก) ส่วน hit the nail on the head แปลว่าพูดถูกเผง ซึ่งเท่ากับยืนยันว่า B ทำพลาด Better late than never และ the last straw ไม่เข้ากับสถานการณ์

items.subject: eng

skill.th: การตอบเมื่อเพื่อนปฏิเสธคำเชิญ

topic.th: บทสนทนาในชีวิตประจำวัน

items.stem:
Choose the best response to complete the conversation.
A: I'm sorry, but I don't think I'll be able to make it to your party on Saturday.
B: ______ Maybe we can get together next weekend instead.
choices: Oh, I'm glad to hear it.

explanation.en: B is disappointed and suggests another time, so "Oh, that's a shame" fits. "Good for you" and "I'm glad to hear it" show pleasure at good news, and "I'll go instead" makes no sense because it is B's own party.
explanation.th: B รู้สึกเสียดายและเสนอนัดใหม่ จึงตอบ Oh, that's a shame ส่วน Good for you และ I'm glad to hear it แสดงความยินดีกับข่าวดี และ I'll go instead ไม่สมเหตุสมผลเพราะเป็นงานของ B เอง

items.subject: eng

skill.th: คำปรากฏร่วมกับ decision

topic.th: คำปรากฏร่วมและกริยาวลี

items.stem:
Choose the best option to complete the sentence.
"We need to ______ a decision about the class trip by Friday."

explanation.en: The usual collocation is "make a decision". Thai learners often choose "do", but we do homework or a job, not a decision; "give" and "put" do not collocate with decision.
explanation.th: คำที่ใช้คู่กันคือ make a decision ผู้เรียนไทยมักใช้ do แต่ do ใช้กับ homework หรือ job ส่วน give และ put ไม่ใช้กับ decision

items.subject: eng

skill.th: การสร้างคำนามที่ลงท้ายด้วย -ity

topic.th: ความหมายคำและการสร้างคำ

items.stem:
Choose the best option to complete the sentence.
"Online shopping has become very popular, but some customers still worry about the ______ of their personal data."

explanation.en: After "the" and before "of" we need a noun: "security". "Secure" is an adjective or verb, "securely" is an adverb and "securing" is a verb form.
explanation.th: หลัง the และก่อน of ต้องเป็นคำนาม คือ security ส่วน secure เป็นคุณศัพท์หรือกริยา securely เป็นกริยาวิเศษณ์ และ securing เป็นรูปกริยา

items.subject: eng

skill.th: คำปรากฏร่วม reach a compromise

topic.th: คำปรากฏร่วมและกริยาวลี

items.stem:
Choose the best option to complete the sentence.
"After months of difficult negotiations, the two countries finally reached a ______ that both sides could accept."

explanation.en: Two sides with different positions "reach a compromise" (an agreement in which each gives up something). A promise is made, not reached; a commitment is made or given; and a dispute is the disagreement itself, not its solution.
explanation.th: สองฝ่ายที่เห็นต่างกันจะ reach a compromise คือบรรลุข้อตกลงที่ต่างฝ่ายต่างยอมกันคนละนิด ส่วน promise และ commitment ใช้กับ make ไม่ใช่ reach และ dispute คือความขัดแย้งเอง ไม่ใช่ทางออก

items.subject: eng

skill.th: คำพ้องความหมายของคุณศัพท์ระดับทางการ

topic.th: ความหมายคำและการสร้างคำ

items.stem:
Choose the word closest in meaning to "compelling".
"The evidence against the suspect was so compelling that the jury needed only an hour to reach a verdict."

explanation.en: The jury decided very quickly, so the evidence must have been strong and persuasive: "compelling" means convincing. Confusing or limited evidence would slow the jury down, and surprising does not explain the quick verdict.
explanation.th: คณะลูกขุนตัดสินได้รวดเร็ว แสดงว่าหลักฐานหนักแน่นน่าเชื่อ compelling จึงแปลว่า convincing ส่วนหลักฐานที่สับสนหรือมีน้อยจะทำให้ตัดสินช้า และ surprising ไม่ได้อธิบายการตัดสินที่รวดเร็ว

items.subject: eng

skill.th: กริยาวลี run into

topic.th: คำปรากฏร่วมและกริยาวลี

items.stem:
Choose the best option to complete the sentence.
"I ran ______ an old classmate at the shopping centre yesterday; I hadn't seen him for years."

explanation.en: "Run into someone" means meet them by chance. "Run out of" means have none left, "run over" means hit with a vehicle, and "run up" means build up a debt or run towards.
explanation.th: run into someone แปลว่าเจอโดยบังเอิญ ส่วน run out of แปลว่าหมด run over แปลว่าขับรถทับ และ run up แปลว่าก่อหนี้หรือวิ่งเข้าไปหา

items.subject: eng

skill.en: Idiomatic expressions: in the nick of time
skill.th: สำนวน in the nick of time

topic.th: คำปรากฏร่วมและกริยาวลี

items.stem:
Choose the best option to complete the sentence.
"Despite the heavy traffic, the ambulance arrived in the ______ of time and the patient was saved."

explanation.en: "In the nick of time" is a fixed idiom meaning just before it was too late. "Edge", "end" and "point" do not form this idiom.
explanation.th: in the nick of time เป็นสำนวนตายตัว แปลว่าทันเวลาพอดี ก่อนจะสายเกินไป ส่วน edge, end, point ไม่ได้ใช้ในสำนวนนี้

items.subject: eng

skill.th: การสร้างกริยาที่ลงท้ายด้วย -ify

topic.th: ความหมายคำและการสร้างคำ

items.stem:
Choose the best option to complete the sentence.
"The teacher tried to ______ her explanation so that the younger students could follow it."

explanation.en: After "tried to" we need a base verb: "simplify" (make simpler). "Simple" is an adjective, "simplicity" a noun and "simply" an adverb.
explanation.th: หลัง tried to ต้องเป็นกริยารูปฐาน คือ simplify (ทำให้ง่ายขึ้น) ส่วน simple เป็นคุณศัพท์ simplicity เป็นคำนาม และ simply เป็นกริยาวิเศษณ์

items.subject: eng

skill.th: คุณศัพท์ + บุพบท addicted to

topic.th: คำปรากฏร่วมและกริยาวลี

items.stem:
Choose the best option to complete the sentence.
"Many young people are ______ to social media, checking their phones hundreds of times a day."

explanation.en: Checking a phone hundreds of times a day shows a habit people cannot stop, and "addicted" takes "to". "Interested" takes "in", and "involved"/"concerned" do not describe this behaviour.
explanation.th: การเช็กโทรศัพท์หลายร้อยครั้งต่อวันแสดงถึงการติดจนเลิกไม่ได้ และ addicted ใช้กับ to ส่วน interested ใช้กับ in และ involved, concerned ไม่ได้บรรยายพฤติกรรมนี้

items.subject: eng

skill.en: 'Be going to' for predictions from evidence
skill.th: be going to สำหรับการคาดการณ์จากหลักฐาน

topic.th: กาลของกริยา

items.stem:
Choose the best option to complete the sentence.
"Look at those dark clouds! It ______ rain any minute."

explanation.en: We can see evidence now (dark clouds), so we use "be going to" for the prediction: "It's going to rain". "Will be rain" is ungrammatical, "rains" is a habit, and "is raining" means it has already started.
explanation.th: เห็นหลักฐานในปัจจุบัน (เมฆดำ) จึงใช้ be going to ในการคาดการณ์ คือ It's going to rain ส่วน will be rain ผิดไวยากรณ์ rains เป็นนิสัยหรือความจริงทั่วไป และ is raining หมายถึงฝนตกอยู่แล้ว

items.subject: eng

skill.th: future perfect continuous

topic.th: กาลของกริยา

items.stem:
Choose the best option to complete the sentence.
"By the time she retires next year, she ______ for the same company for twenty years."

explanation.en: "By the time … next year" looks back from a future point at a continuing period (for twenty years), so the future perfect continuous "will have been working" is needed. The other forms do not reach to that future point.
explanation.th: By the time … next year มองย้อนจากจุดเวลาในอนาคตไปยังช่วงเวลาที่ต่อเนื่อง (for twenty years) จึงต้องใช้ future perfect continuous คือ will have been working ส่วนรูปอื่นไม่ได้ต่อเนื่องถึงจุดเวลาในอนาคตนั้น

items.subject: eng

skill.en: Mixed conditional: present condition, past result
skill.th: mixed conditional เงื่อนไขปัจจุบัน ผลในอดีต

topic.th: ประโยคเงื่อนไขและ wish

items.stem:
Choose the best option to complete the sentence.
"If Napat weren't so shy, he ______ for class president last month."

explanation.en: Being shy is a present, general fact (weren't), but the result is in the past (last month), so we use "would have run". "Would run" refers to now, and "will run"/"had run" do not form a conditional result.
explanation.th: ความขี้อายเป็นลักษณะในปัจจุบัน (weren't) แต่ผลอยู่ในอดีต (last month) จึงใช้ would have run ส่วน would run หมายถึงปัจจุบัน และ will run, had run ไม่ใช่รูปผลของประโยคเงื่อนไข

items.subject: eng

skill.en: 'If only' + past simple for present wishes
skill.th: If only + past simple ความปรารถนาในปัจจุบัน

topic.th: ประโยคเงื่อนไขและ wish

items.stem:
Choose the best option to complete the sentence.
"If only I ______ how to swim! Then I could join my friends at the beach."

explanation.en: The wish is about now ("Then I could join…"), so "if only" takes the past simple: "knew". "Had known" is for past regrets, "know" is not used after if only, and "would know" is not used for one's own abilities.
explanation.th: ความปรารถนานี้เป็นเรื่องปัจจุบัน (Then I could join…) If only จึงตามด้วย past simple คือ knew ส่วน had known ใช้เสียดายเรื่องในอดีต know ใช้หลัง if only ไม่ได้ และ would know ไม่ใช้กับความสามารถของตนเอง

items.subject: eng

skill.th: passive กับ modal perfect

topic.th: ประโยค passive และ causative

items.stem:
Choose the best option to complete the sentence.
"The accident ______ if the driver had been paying attention."

explanation.en: This is an unreal past situation (third conditional), and the accident is avoided by someone, so we need modal + have been + past participle: "could have been avoided". "Could have avoided" is active and would make the accident avoid something.
explanation.th: เป็นสถานการณ์ที่ไม่จริงในอดีต (เงื่อนไขแบบที่ 3) และอุบัติเหตุถูกหลีกเลี่ยง จึงต้องใช้ modal + have been + V3 คือ could have been avoided ส่วน could have avoided เป็น active ทำให้อุบัติเหตุกลายเป็นผู้หลีกเลี่ยง

items.subject: eng

skill.th: การสลับที่หลัง Only after

topic.th: ความสอดคล้อง การเปรียบเทียบ และการสลับที่

items.stem:
Choose the best option to complete the sentence.
"Only after the results were announced ______ how close the competition had been."

explanation.en: "Only after + clause" at the start of a sentence causes inversion in the main clause: auxiliary + subject + verb, "did we realise". The other choices keep normal order or put the subject after the main verb.
explanation.th: เมื่อขึ้นต้นด้วย Only after + อนุประโยค ประโยคหลักต้องสลับที่เป็นกริยาช่วย + ประธาน + กริยา คือ did we realise ส่วนตัวเลือกอื่นเรียงแบบปกติหรือวางประธานหลังกริยาแท้

items.subject: eng

skill.th: causative get something done

topic.th: ประโยค passive และ causative

items.stem:
Choose the best option to complete the sentence.
"I'm going to ______ before the graduation ceremony."

explanation.en: A hairdresser will do it, so we use get + object + past participle: "get my hair cut". The object must come before the participle, "to cut" is wrong, and "have cut my hair" means I cut it myself (perfect tense).
explanation.th: ช่างตัดผมเป็นผู้ตัดให้ จึงใช้ get + กรรม + V3 คือ get my hair cut กรรมต้องอยู่หน้า V3 ส่วน to cut ผิด และ have cut my hair เป็น perfect tense หมายถึงตัดเอง

items.subject: eng

skill.th: participle clause รูป V3 (ความหมาย passive)

topic.th: อนุประโยคสัมพันธ์และ participle clause

items.stem:
Choose the best option to complete the sentence.
"______ in 1782, Bangkok has been Thailand's capital for more than two centuries."

explanation.en: Bangkok was founded by someone, so the clause is passive: the past participle "Founded". "Founding" and "Having founded" are active and would mean Bangkok founded something; "To found" shows purpose.
explanation.th: กรุงเทพฯ ถูกสถาปนา จึงต้องใช้รูป passive คือ Founded ส่วน Founding และ Having founded เป็น active หมายถึงกรุงเทพฯ เป็นผู้ก่อตั้ง และ To found แสดงจุดประสงค์

items.subject: eng

skill.th: คำพูดรายงานในประโยคเงื่อนไข

topic.en: Verb patterns, modals and reported speech
topic.th: รูปแบบกริยา modal และคำพูดรายงาน

items.stem:
Choose the best option to complete the sentence.
"Last season, the coach warned us that if we ______ late again, we would not be allowed to play."

explanation.en: The coach's words were "If you are late again, you won't be allowed…"; in reported speech after "warned", "are" moves back to "were" and "won't" to "would not". "Will" and "would" are not used in the if-clause.
explanation.th: คำพูดเดิมคือ If you are late again, you won't be allowed… เมื่อรายงานหลัง warned กาลจะถอยหลัง are เป็น were และ won't เป็น would not ส่วน will และ would ไม่ใช้ในอนุประโยค if

items.subject: eng

skill.th: needn't have + V3

topic.en: Verb patterns, modals and reported speech
topic.th: รูปแบบกริยา modal และคำพูดรายงาน

items.stem:
Choose the best option to complete the sentence.
"You ______ have bought me a present — but thank you, it's lovely!"

explanation.en: "Needn't have bought" means you did buy it, but it was not necessary, which fits the thanks that follow. "Mustn't have" is not used for the past, "don't need have" is ungrammatical, and "couldn't have bought" would mean it was impossible.
explanation.th: needn't have bought หมายถึงซื้อมาแล้วแต่จริง ๆ ไม่จำเป็นต้องซื้อ ซึ่งเข้ากับคำขอบคุณที่ตามมา ส่วน mustn't have ไม่ใช้กับอดีต don't need have ผิดไวยากรณ์ และ couldn't have bought แปลว่าเป็นไปไม่ได้ที่จะซื้อ

items.subject: eng

skill.th: ความสอดคล้องเมื่อใช้ each of

items.stem:

items.passage:
Farms in the Sky

Imagine a farm with no fields, no tractors and no sunshine. Instead, there are rows of shelves stacked twelve levels high inside a warehouse, each one covered with lettuce, basil or strawberries growing under purple LED lights. This is vertical farming, and its supporters believe it could change the way cities feed themselves.

The idea is simple. Rather than spreading crops across a large area of land, vertical farms grow them upwards, in a building where every condition can be controlled. Temperature, humidity and light are adjusted by computers twenty-four hours a day. Because the plants are grown indoors, there are few insects to fight, so farmers rarely need pesticides. Most vertical farms also use hydroponics, a method in which roots are fed by water containing nutrients rather than by soil. This system recycles the water, using up to ninety per cent less than a traditional farm.

Location is another advantage. A vertical farm can be built in the middle of a city, close to supermarkets and restaurants. Vegetables can be picked in the morning and sold the same afternoon, which means they are fresher and less food is wasted during transport.

However, vertical farming is not the perfect solution it is sometimes made out to be. The biggest problem is energy. Sunlight is free, but LED lights and air-conditioning are not, and several well-funded vertical farming companies have gone out of business because their electricity bills were simply too high. Critics also point out that the method works well only for small, fast-growing plants such as salad leaves and herbs. Staple crops like rice, wheat and potatoes need far more space and light, and growing them indoors would be extremely expensive.

For now, then, vertical farms are unlikely to replace traditional agriculture. Instead, they may become a useful addition to it, especially in crowded, wealthy cities where land is scarce and consumers are willing to pay more for fresh, pesticide-free vegetables. If renewable energy becomes much cheaper, however, the picture could change dramatically.
items.stem: Which title best summarises the passage?
choices: Why LED Lights Are Bad for Plants

explanation.en: The passage presents advantages (water, pesticides, freshness) and serious limits (energy, crop types), concluding that vertical farms are a useful addition, not a replacement. It says rice is too expensive to grow indoors, rejects the end of traditional farming, and never says LEDs harm plants.

The Wallet

The wallet was lying in a puddle beside the bus stop, its brown leather turning almost black in the rain. Krit picked it up without thinking and opened it. Inside were three thousand-baht notes, an ID card, a photograph of a little girl in a school uniform, and a folded receipt from a hospital.

Three thousand baht. Krit stared at the money for longer than he would have liked to admit. His phone screen had been cracked for months, and his parents had already told him that a new one would have to wait until after the rice harvest. Nobody had seen him pick the wallet up. The bus stop was empty, and the street was hidden behind a curtain of rain.

Then he looked at the photograph again. The girl had a gap between her front teeth and was holding up a certificate with both hands, grinning as if she had just won the world. Krit unfolded the receipt. It was for a medical test, and at the bottom someone had written in pen: "Results Monday — don't forget!"

He sighed, put the wallet in his bag and, instead of going home, walked twenty minutes in the opposite direction to the police station. The officer at the desk wrote down his name, telephone number and school, and told him that he could go.

On Monday morning, the whole of Matthayom 3 was called to the assembly hall to meet a new mathematics teacher who had transferred from the north. She was a small woman with a soft voice, and she began by saying that she wanted to tell them a story before she taught them a single equation. "On Friday," she said, "I lost something very important in the rain. It contained money I had saved for my daughter's operation. I was sure I would never see it again." She paused and looked down at a piece of paper in her hand. "Is there a student here called Krit Wongsa?"

Krit felt three hundred faces turn towards him at once. He had never wanted the floor to swallow him so much in his life—and he had never felt so proud.

He was tempted to keep the money for a new phone.

He thought the wallet belonged to a classmate.

explanation.en: Krit stared at the money, thought about his cracked phone, and noticed that nobody had seen him: he was tempted. Nothing suggests fear of the police, he walked straight to the station, and he did not know the owner.

Let Teenagers Work

In many Thai families, a teenager with a part-time job is seen as a sign that something has gone wrong. Parents worry that work will take time away from tutoring and homework, and that it will damage their child's chances of getting into a good university. I understand these fears, but I believe they are mostly mistaken. A few hours of paid work each week can teach young people lessons that no classroom can.

The first of these is the value of money. A student who has spent a Saturday afternoon serving coffee for a modest hourly wage thinks very differently about a 2,000-baht pair of trainers. Abstract numbers become hours of real effort, and teenagers who have earned their own money tend to spend it more carefully.

Work also builds skills that employers—and universities—increasingly value. Dealing with an impatient customer, cooperating with colleagues twice your age and arriving on time without a parent waking you up are not things that can be learned from a textbook. These so-called "soft skills" are exactly what many companies say young graduates lack.

Critics point to studies showing that students who work long hours get lower grades. The key word here is "long". Research consistently finds that the problems begin when teenagers work more than fifteen or twenty hours a week during the school term. Below that level, the effect on grades is small, and some studies even find that working students manage their time better than their classmates. Nobody is suggesting that a fifteen-year-old should work every evening; I am arguing that one or two shifts a week should be seen as normal, not shameful.

There is also a question of fairness. For many young people from poorer families, a part-time job is not a choice but a necessity. When we treat working teenagers as a problem, we send these students the message that they are somehow less serious about their future. Surely we should be doing the opposite.

Of course, employers must follow the law, which protects young workers from dangerous jobs and late-night hours. But within those limits, let teenagers work. They may learn more from a year behind a counter than from another year of weekend tutoring.
items.stem: What is the writer's main purpose?
choices: To warn parents about the dangers of part-time jobs
To explain Thai labour laws in detail
To persuade readers that a limited amount of part-time work is good for teenagers

explanation.en: The title and the repeated argument ("a few hours", "one or two shifts a week") show the writer is persuading readers to accept limited part-time work. The writer disagrees with the warnings, mentions the law only briefly, and does not compare tutoring schools.
